ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows triangle ABC with A at the top, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right. Point D lies on side AB. Segment CD is drawn from C to D, and the angle marks at C indicate that CD bisects angle C. Tick marks indicate CD = BC. The unknown angle is angle CDA at point D between DC and DA. Let the equal base angles of the isosceles triangle ABC be x. Since AB = AC, the base is BC, so ∠ABC = ∠BCA = x. Because CD bisects angle C, ∠BCD = ∠DCA = x/2. Also, D lies on AB and CD = BC. In triangle BCD, sides BC and CD are equal, so the opposite angles are equal: ∠CBD = ∠BDC. Since D lies on AB, ray BD lies along BA, so ∠CBD = ∠CBA = x. Therefore ∠BDC = x. Now sum the angles in triangle BCD: x + x + x/2 = 180°, so 5x/2 = 180°, giving x = 72°. Finally, ∠CDA and ∠CDB are a linear pair on line AB, so ∠CDA = 180° − 72° = 108°.

Because D is on AB, ∠CBD is the same as ∠CBA, hence ∠CBD=x and therefore ∠BDC=x. Sum angles in triangle BCD: x+x+x/2=180°, giving x=72°.
